claim.locator: abstract of the collaboration's 1997 summary paper (Hyperfine Interactions 109, 191)
claim.quote: The production of eleven antihydrogen atoms is reported including possibly 2 ± 1 background signals, the observed yield agrees with theoretical predictions.

date.locator: opening line of CERN's press release
date.note: Announcement date: CERN's press release of 4 January 1996 (production in September 1995). The Physics Letters B paper is dated February 1996 (Crossref); its abstract could not be retrieved verbatim, so the claim quote is taken from the collaboration's own 1997 summary abstract.

key_value_text.quote: The production of eleven antihydrogen atoms is reported including possibly 2 ± 1 background signals
key_value_text.value: Eleven antihydrogen atoms including possibly 2 ± 1 background signals (collaboration summary); CERN announced nine atoms

name: Production of antihydrogen
notes: Number of atoms: the CERN press release says nine atoms; the collaboration's 1997 abstract says eleven including possibly 2 ± 1 background signals. Both are reported; the later collaboration wording is used for the claim.

significance.quote: the observed yield agrees with theoretical predictions
significance.value: Eleven candidate events including possibly 2 ± 1 background signals; yield agrees with theoretical predictions

summary.plain: The PS210 experiment made the first atoms of antimatter: antiprotons circulating in a CERN storage ring passed through xenon gas and a few combined with a positron. CERN announced nine atoms in 1996; the collaboration later reported eleven candidates including possible background.
summary.technical: Antihydrogen produced in flight in antiproton collisions with xenon in LEAR, mediated by e+e− pair creation via two photons; atoms identified by a unique detector signature. The collaboration reports eleven antihydrogen atoms including possibly 2 ± 1 background signals; the observed yield agrees with theory.

title: Production of antihydrogen
why_it_matters: The collaboration says it concentrated on production because antihydrogen had not been observed before; in principle it is well suited to fundamental CPT-violation studies.
